articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia ramping up attacks to ‘pressure’ Kyiv at trilateral talks, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary:
President urges US for support, saying ‘Ukraine must not be left to face this alone’ as barrage plunges cities into darkness. What we know on day 1,719

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop. “By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to additionally lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine’s position and that of its partners,” the Ukrainian president said. “Russia perceives diplomacy in its own peculiar way – as a form of aggression.”

Ukraine’s energy ministry said “a massive attack on a number of energy facilities” on Saturday had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding regions. Russia had throughout the night launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, Zelenskyy said, among which were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea.

The strikes came before a US-brokered trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for next week aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace. Ukrainian officials are expected to sit down with Russian negotiators and US envoys on Tuesday and Wednesday for the first such talks in months. The diplomatic track has been stalled since February when Washington shifted attention to its war with Iran.

Zelenskyy also urged the US to increase its flagging aid to Ukraine. “Unfortunately, there is still a significant shortage of interceptors for Patriot systems, and the United States is in the best position to help address it,” he said.

Italy’s foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, on Saturday said he had been targeted by pro-Russian hackers over his backing for Ukraine. Tajani said in a post on X that “backing in a transparent way the freedom and independence of a sovereign state” had made him a target. Tajani said his personal data had been published on the dark web and that the hackers were seeking further information about him and his family and were ‌willing to pay for it.

The Italian prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who has been one of the strongest backers of Ukraine among western leaders, expressed her support for Tajani and said the sale of confidential information relating to public officials was “a matter of serious concern”. Moscow has not commented ‌on the incident. ‌

France’s far-left presidential contender Jean-Luc Mélenchon said on Saturday that settling the Ukraine conflict could not be done by granting territorial concessions without consulting the people concerned. Melenchon, who polls suggest could reach the second round of next year’s presidential election, set out his France Unbowed party’s foreign policy positions at a rally just outside Paris.

Mélenchon has been criticised in the past for questioning the legitimacy of Zelenskyy. But in a campaign speech to thousands of supporters, he said an administration run by his party would take an active role in settling the war in Ukraine. Europe would have to play an active role in peace talks, he said. “We cannot accept that one could consider a peace with territorial concessions in Ukraine without asking the populations concerned if they agree or not to be on one side or other of the border,” he said. “It is for the people themselves to decide what they want,” he added.

A Ukrainian attack killed one person in Russia’s Belgorod region when a drone hit a private home in the town of Grayvoron, local officials said on Saturday. Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down 411 Ukrainian drones overnight over 10 Russian regions, including Belgorod. Drones were also destroyed over the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black and Azov seas, it said. Russian media outlets later reported that the Saratov Oil Refinery had been hit and shared images of plumes of smoke over the city.

Na geopolitické scéně eskalují dopady amerických politických zvratů na transatlantické vztahy a ukrajinský konflikt pokračuje s vysokou intenzitou ruských útoků na civilní infrastrukturu.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a wave of domestic social unrest, protests, and strikes in countries like France, while persistent inflation pressures keep the European Central Bank on course for further monetary policy tightening. On the geopolitical front, the spillover effects of US political shifts on transatlantic relations are escalating, and the war in Ukraine continues with intense Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující stávkovou vlnu a protesty v západní Evropě, zostřenou pozornost vůči kybernetické bezpečnosti kritické infrastruktury a napjaté vyjednávání o financování ukrajinské pomoci mimo rámec rozpočtu EU.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further waves of strikes and protests in Western Europe, heightened focus on critical infrastructure cybersecurity, and tense negotiations over financing aid to Ukraine outside the EU budget framework can be expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí eskalujícím sociálním nepokojům, vlnám stávek v západních zemích kvůli životním nákladům a pokračujícím fatálním útokům na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu. Politickou scénu navíc komplikují mocenské boje v Německu před volbami a blížící se odchod prezidentky ECB Christine Lagardeové v únoru 2027.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing escalating social unrest, waves of strikes in Western countries driven by the cost of living, and ongoing fatal attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Furthermore, the political landscape is complicated by power struggles in Germany ahead of elections and the upcoming departure of ECB President Christine Lagarde in February 2027.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, mass protests against the cost of living in Western Europe and intensified diplomatic pressure for energy equipment supplies to Ukraine are expected to continue. Markets will remain nervous due to developments in the US and monetary policy.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí akutním bezpečnostním hrozbám v čele s koordinovanou vlnou pumových hrozeb na komerční lety a mediální domy, přičemž geopolitické napětí eskaluje v souvislosti s konfliktem na Ukrajině a situací v Hormuzském průlivu. Politická nestabilita se projevuje i v členských státech skrze radikalizaci, sociální pnutí a regulační tlaky Evropské komise na technologické giganty.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing acute security threats led by a coordinated wave of bomb threats targeting commercial flights and media houses, while geopolitical tensions escalate over the war in Ukraine and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Political instability is also manifesting across member states through radicalization, social friction, and the European Commission's regulatory pressures on tech giants.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřená bezpečnostní opatření na evropských letištích a diplomatické manévry kolem nadcházejících summitů v Dublinu. Finanční trhy zůstanou citlivé na vývoj v oblasti energetiky a geopolitických třenic.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened security measures at European airports and diplomatic maneuvers surrounding upcoming summits in Dublin are expected. Financial markets will remain sensitive to developments in energy and geopolitical friction.

Prezidentská klání a politické posuny, včetně souboje o nástupnictví v ECB mezi Španělskem a Nizozemskem, zvyšují makroekonomickou i politickou nestabilitu v regionu.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces a mounting wave of hybrid threats, critical infrastructure sabotage, and anti-AI protests, while Middle Eastern tensions and the war in Ukraine continue to strain security. Political shifts and the ECB leadership contest between Spain and the Netherlands add to regional macroeconomic and political instability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřená bezpečnostní opatření v souvislosti s vyšetřováním bombových hrozeb a pokračující debaty o nástupnictví v čele ECB. Finanční trhy budou citlivě reagovat na vývoj v energetice a technologickém sektoru.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened security measures regarding bomb threat investigations and ongoing debates over ECB leadership are expected. Financial markets will remain sensitive to developments in energy and the tech sector.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí zvýšenému napětí kvůli pokračujícím ruským útokům na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu a financování obrany, přičemž NATO registruje významný schodek v přislíbené vojenské pomoci. Bezpečnostní situaci na kontinentu navíc zhoršují vnitrostátní incidenty, jako je krvavý útok pravicového extremisty v polském Krakově a rostoucí sociální napětí kolem migrace.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing heightened tension due to ongoing Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and defense funding gaps, with NATO registering a significant shortfall in pledged military aid. The continent's security landscape is further strained by domestic incidents, such as the deadly far-right shooting rampage in Kraków, Poland, and rising social tensions over migration.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává stupňující se diplomatické i vojenské napětí kolem Ukrajiny a zostřená bezpečnostní opatření v Polsku po tragické střelbě v Krakově. Finanční trhy budou sledovat politické manévry ohledně budoucího vedení ECB.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, escalating diplomatic and military tensions around Ukraine and heightened security measures in Poland following the tragic Kraków shooting are expected. Financial markets will closely monitor political maneuvers regarding future ECB leadership.
